rows: Darling, I know you're wonderful on the mat. Getting me there is the part of the performance you haven't rehearsed.
A spectacular noise when you hit someone. A pity noise alone doesn't decide the final act.
What a lovely view you must have from up there. I'll be arranging the reception when you come down.
You can keep the audience in suspense. You cannot keep me waiting all evening.
These people dressed up, came out and paid for a show. Let's give them the whole performance.
I could talk all night, but I'd rather you saw the good bit in the ring.
The running order is a charming suggestion. The main event begins with my entrance.
Take a good look. This is what you're being asked to compete with.
Avoid the mat if you like. I'll introduce you to it in my own time.
You make that sound terribly sensible. I wonder how it sounds after the first hit.
The trick is knowing where I intend to land. You haven't got the script.
Suspense is an art, darling. Try not to rush the ending.
An admirable sentiment. Let's see whether you can sustain the performance.
You've claimed the headline. How lovely. Shall we ask the audience?
Your {strength}. Yes, I was listening. I'll arrange my performance around the obstacle.
I don't intend to pretend your {strength} aren't impressive. I intend to make something more memorable happen.
I have nothing against you personally. I simply have no intention of sharing the victory.
Let's not compete for volume. That's a dreadful way to spend the evening.
I could make a scene. I prefer to make an entrance.
One fall, two performers, no supporting cast.
Come on then, take me to the mat and demonstrate this marvellous technique.
Stay on the canvas a little longer. Let's see what you can do without the high lights.
Don't leave the stage through the ropes halfway through our scene.
Perfect. At last we agree on something.
You've delivered a lovely diversion. Now answer the question.
I'll grant you that. Don't get carried away.
I anticipate a demanding performance. I'll be the one who wins it.
One clean fall, centre stage. No cheap tricks.
That's the end of my speech. Enjoy the show.
I've got a little something in mind. No spoilers.
What a dreadful line that was. I haven't got a particular incident to support it, so let's cut it from the performance.
I can make a scene, darling. I cannot make an accusation true by delivering it beautifully.
Wonderful. We can dispense with that scene and give them the main attraction.
A fair correction. No unsupported scandal required; we have a match to perform.
Darling, the audience can judge whether either of us delivers a performance worthy of the billing. No invented scandal required.
Let them watch the final act and see who has earned the curtain call. That's a verdict I can live with.
